title: Leaky Mutability (Shared State Leak)
pattern: Exposing a direct, mutable reference to an internal private collection, allowing external callers to perform arbitrary mutations without the struct's knowledge.
why_bad: It breaks the encapsulation of the struct entirely. Callers can bypass any validations or invariants that the struct is designed to enforce on its collection, leading to corrupt or invalid states.
detection: A method returning a mutable reference (`&mut`) to a private field of type `Vec`, `HashMap`, or any collection.
counterexample: Conceptually open collection wrappers or builders whose explicit purpose is to act as customizable containers.
fix: Return read-only references (e.g., `&[T]`), perform mutations strictly via encapsulating methods (e.g., `register_user`), or return clones.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 6, Section 6.2 ("Minimize accessibility"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17.
